images.title: The carries of 176 × 24
images.purpose: Show where the carries go when 176 is multiplied by 24: the carries of the ones row sit above the next places, the carries of the tens row sit above them, and the two rows add to the total.
images.composition: One ledger with four place columns: two rows of carry circles above the number 176, the multiplier 24 under it, the two rows of small products, the total, and a caption.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. A ledger of 4 place columns, each 180 px wide: thousands x 330 to 510 (centre 420), hundreds x 510 to 690 (centre 600), tens x 690 to 870 (centre 780), ones x 870 to 1050 (centre 960). All text is dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif. At y 60 the four column heads, centred in their columns (30 px): thousands, hundreds, tens, ones. CARRY CIRCLES (each 56 px across with a 3 px outline and a digit inside, 34 px): in the row at y 135, two green #009E73 circles, one in the hundreds column (x 600) holding 1 and one in the tens column (x 780) holding 1; in the row at y 205, two reddish purple #CC79A7 circles, one in the hundreds column (x 600) holding 3 and one in the tens column (x 780) holding 2. The number 176 at y 290 (56 px): the digit 1 in the hundreds column, 7 in the tens column and 6 in the ones column. The multiplier at y 370 (56 px): the sign × at x 280, the digit 2 in the tens column and 4 in the ones column. A dark #2B2B2B rule (4 px) at y 410 from x 270 to x 1050. Row 1 at y 470 (56 px): 7 in the hundreds column, 0 in the tens column and 4 in the ones column. Row 2 at y 550 (56 px): the sign + at x 280, then 3 in the thousands column, 5 in the hundreds column, 2 in the tens column and 0 in the ones column; the 0 in the ones column is grey #6B7280 because it is the zero placed first. A dark rule (4 px) at y 595 from x 270 to x 1050. The total at y 665 (60 px, bold): 4 in the thousands column, 2 in the hundreds column, 2 in the tens column and 4 in the ones column. Labels at the right, left aligned at x 1100 (30 px): at y 135 carries for 2 tens, at y 205 carries for 4, at y 470 row 1: 4 × 176, at y 550 row 2: 2 tens × 176. Centred at x 728 and y 752 the caption 176 × 24 = 704 + 3,520 = 4,224 (40 px, bold). No other text. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a carry circle in a column other than the one listed, or a carry circle with a digit other than the one listed
a total other than 4 2 2 4, a row 1 other than 7 0 4, or a row 2 other than 3 5 2 0
images.takeaway: Each carry goes above the next place to the left and is added after that place is multiplied, so the rows 704 and 3,520 add to 4,224.
images.description: A ledger for 176 × 24 with the carry circles 2 and 3 for the ones row and 1 and 1 for the tens row, the rows 704 and 3,520 and the total 4,224.
images.context: Concept image for Carry to the Right Place. It follows the idea of Mili's father's place value table in your maths book (carry circles above the number, one row for each digit of the multiplier) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example: 176 and 24.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student follow each carry from the product that makes it to the circle above the next place. The slip to watch: adding the carry to the digit before multiplying it.

image_decisions.why: The ledger with its carry circles is the method: it shows which place each carry goes to, which words alone do not.
